ONE-TRUTH-1 made 19 copies machine-written and machine-checked. That was the wrong shape: a
generated copy is still a copy, it still has to be kept in step, and a reader who finds one has
no way to know whether it is the truth or a stale rendering of it. ONE-TRUTH-2 (the owner's
order) deleted all 19. Where a document's argument needed the reader to know a fingerprint
EXISTS, it now points here; where it did not, the mention was removed.
WHERE A CURRENT VALUE MAY STILL APPEAR, and nowhere else:
- this file
- docs/TAGS.md — the tag register. A tag's hash is what it was when the tag was cut.
- reports/ — the lab journal. Append-only by rule: a report records what was true on the day
it was written and must never be rewritten. Listed as a PREFIX rather than 112 filenames,
which is a decision: enumerating them would be noise that nobody would maintain, and the
append-only rule already makes every one of them history by construction.
TO RE-MINT: run the role's `reproduce` command, put the new value here, and commit. There is
nothing else to update — that is the point.
WHICH DOCUMENT OWNS WHAT, resolved because four of them implied they owned this:
- THIS FILE owns the CURRENT VALUES. Nothing else does.
- docs/SIM.md owns the LINEAGE — which change moved which value to which. Its head points here.
- reports/parity/REBASELINE.md owns WHAT MOVED each one, and now carries no values.
- docs/SHIP-CEREMONY.md owns the PROCEDURE for minting.

camera.covers: the DIRECTOR's decisions: state, phase, anchor, zoom, offsets, camT, targets — INCLUDING the ending the director composes after the last crossing (CAMERA-ENDING-WINDOW-1)
camera.mintedBy: SHIP-RUNIN-CALM-1 — THE OWNER JUDGED THE RUN-IN ON A PRODUCTION BUILD ON 2026-08-26 AND ACCEPTED IT: the closing phase is calm. This hash is that acceptance written down. TWO REPAIRS, EACH WITH ITS CAUSE FOUND BEFORE IT WAS BUILT. (1) RUNIN-PIVOT-SCOPE-1 — the aim was RESOLVED at the previous frame's zoom and DRAWN at this one's, because `_setTrackTargets` answered how WIDE and where to AIM in one pass while the frame's zoom was settled afterwards. Split at the seam that already existed: `_resolvePanTarget()` now runs after `update()` has settled the zoom on every path. That deleted two of the five compensating corrections the file carried. THE TWO ZOOM-ABOUT-THE-ANCHOR PIVOTS STAY and are bounded on both sides — deleting them costs 59 px -> 360 px of sideways jump (RUNIN-ORDER-FIX-1 measured it and stopped that piece), widening them to the entry path costs the level-set guarantee 48 cut frames. (2) RUNIN-EASED-ADMIT-1 — the level ceiling had no continuity contract at any of its three boundaries: it admitted by a member's full demand in one frame; its ease anchored ONCE and re-projected any target change by the elapsed fraction (river-run seed 18, ceiling 1.3703 -> 2.4251, x1.77, WHILE the ease was already running); and it was DROPPED outright when the run-in stopped composing (mountainstreet seed 32, guaranteed 1.3139 -> 4.0, x3.05, at the crossing). `preLevel` is smooth across every one of those frames, so the discontinuity was never the demand's own. One rule now: re-anchor whenever the target moves, ease both directions in log space over the same `runInOpenMs`, and leave by ARRIVING rather than vanishing. NO KEY WAS ADDED BY ANY OF IT. RESULT, in the unit he can picture: the largest single-frame movement of the picture at the frame corner falls from 580.58 px to 9.73 px on river-run seed 18 and 368.65 -> 10.05 on seed 13; the largest sideways movement of the subject falls from 59.07 px to under 1.5 px; and ZERO of 100 races carry a movement the strand's own rule calls noticeable, where two did. CONFIRMED ON TEN TRACKS, TEN RACES EACH, INCLUDING GARDEN-PATH — excluded from every previous corpus because the harness could not finish it, and now the CALMEST of the ten at 13.05 px. Three fast tracks (space-sprint 66.69 px seed 2, city-circuit 35.34, ice-track 35.21) are recorded as an OPEN QUESTION rather than averaged in: they are the endgame schedule's own closing rate, not the level ceiling, and they fail the >5x-median half of the perceptibility rule. WORLD AND WORLD-OFF WERE MEASURED, NOT ARGUED, and both came back byte-identical (bc01b74fd4f3cfc8 / daf78ff18eca83c6), which is the check that a run-in repair touches no race.
